vo: This ticket adds a South African ID number to a signup form. No one has asked why it's needed, how long it's kept, or whether privacy signed off.
When a developer starts work, Preflight holds the ticket, before a single line of code is written. The message names the rule, the POPIA sections, and exactly what's missing.
The panel tells you what to do next, and who approves. Every rule shows exactly why it matched.
Rovo drafts the answers with you. But a draft never counts until you confirm it. AI can help. It can't approve.
Your Information Officer sees everything waiting in one inbox, and signs off.
Rewording the ticket won't make the review disappear. And if anyone changes an approved answer, the approval goes stale, and the gate closes again.
Before Done, a second gate asks for proof that it shipped as agreed: the updated privacy notice.
Rules come from your own policy. Rovo turns a policy page into draft rules, and nothing is enforced until an approver activates them. Preflight even shows any workflow that can still skip the gate.
Scanners find personal data after it's already in Jira. Checklists hope someone ticks the box. Preflight puts your privacy review in front of the work, with a write-once record of every decision.
Preflight. Your privacy policy, enforced before build.
